equation_request.abstract: A modification of Tulsi’s quantum search algorithm with intermediate measurements of the control is presented. In order to analyze the effect of measurements in quantum searches, a different choice of the angular parameter is used. The study is performed for several values of time lapses between measurements, finding close relationships between probabilities and correlations (Mutual Information and Cumulative Correlation Measure). The order of this modified algorithm is estimated, showing that for some time lapses the performance is improved, and became of order $O(N)$ (classical brute force search) when the measurement is taken in every step. The results indicate a possible way to analyze improvements to other quantum algorithms using one, or more, control qubits.

specification.problem: Spatial quantum search (Tulsi-type walk search with one control/ancilla qubit) on an N-vertex graph for a single marked vertex w, modified so that the control qubit is projectively measured every tau steps; quantify the success probability, control-walker correlations (mutual information, cumulative correlation measure) and the scaling exponent of the optimal search time with N as a function of tau and of the angular parameter delta.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One smallest useful instance chosen as an assumption: a 2D periodic grid of sqrt(N) x sqrt(N) with N = 16 (4 position qubits), a 2-qubit coin, one control qubit (7 qubits total), a single marked vertex w, a fixed angular parameter delta, and measurement lapses tau in {1, 2, T} where tau = T means no intermediate measurement. The scope covers: state space and initial state, a schematic Tulsi-like step unitary U_delta, the control-measurement channel applied every tau steps, the success probability, the control-walker mutual information, and the operational definition of the scaling exponent. Outside scope (paper contributions not reconstructable from the abstract): the paper's specific 'different choice' of delta, the exact definition of the Cumulative Correlation Measure, the specific set of tau and N values, the reported numerical probability/correlation relationships, and the precise order estimates for each tau other than the stated O(N) for tau = 1.

symbols.meaning: Number of vertices (search space size); for the chosen instance N = 16 on a 4 x 4 periodic grid
Angular parameter of the control-qubit rotation in Tulsi's algorithm (paper uses a non-standard choice, value not given in abstract)
Time lapse (number of walk steps) between successive measurements of the control qubit
Total number of walk steps run
Joint (generally mixed) state of control, coin and position registers after t steps
Single-qubit rotation by angle delta acting on the control qubit
Flip-flop shift operator of the coined walk on the grid
Coin operator (Grover diffusion on the 4-dimensional coin)
Probability of finding the walker at the marked vertex when the position register is measured at time t
Quantum mutual information between the control qubit and the walker (coin+position) at time t
Optimal (first-maximum or threshold) search time as a function of N
Scaling exponent of T^*(N) \propto N^{\alpha}; alpha = 1 corresponds to classical brute-force O(N)

equations.label: Initial state
equations.description: Control qubit in |0>, coin and position registers in uniform superposition; register order is control (most significant) ⊗ coin ⊗ position, position x = n*x_1 + x_2 with n = sqrt(N) encoded in binary.
equations.justification: Standard initial state for coined-walk spatial search algorithms including Tulsi's; the abstract does not state the initial state.
assumptions: Control qubit initialised to |0>; Tulsi's original may use a different control basis convention
Uniform superposition over position and coin

equations.label: Tulsi-like step unitary with control rotation
equations.latex: U_\delta = \big(I_C\otimes S\big)\big(I_C \otimes C \otimes I_{pos}\big)\Big(R_\delta\otimes I_{coin}\otimes|w\rangle\langle w| + I_C\otimes I_{coin}\otimes (I_{pos}-|w\rangle\langle w|)\Big),\qquad R_\delta = \begin{pmatrix}\cos\delta & -\sin\delta\\ \sin\delta & \cos\delta\end{pmatrix}
equations.description: One step: a rotation by delta on the control qubit conditioned on the walker being at the marked vertex, followed by the coin and flip-flop shift. In Tulsi's original algorithm the coin action is additionally controlled by the control qubit; this schematic form is only a placeholder for the exact operator.
equations.justification: The abstract names Tulsi's algorithm and an angular parameter but gives no operator; this is a schematic reconstruction of a controlled rotation entering the walk step, marked as an assumption because the exact Tulsi operator and the paper's modification of delta are not available here.
assumptions: Exact structure of Tulsi's controlled coin/shift is not reproduced; only the delta-rotation on the control conditioned on the marked vertex is modeled
Coin C is the 4-dimensional Grover diffusion operator; S is the flip-flop shift on the periodic grid
Value of delta chosen by the paper ('a different choice') is unknown and must be set as a free parameter

equations.label: Evolution with intermediate control measurements every tau steps
equations.latex: \mathcal{M}(\rho) = \sum_{b\in\{0,1\}} \big(|b\rangle\langle b|_C\otimes I\big)\,\rho\,\big(|b\rangle\langle b|_C\otimes I\big),\qquad \rho_{k\tau} = \mathcal{M}\big(U_\delta^{\tau}\,\rho_{(k-1)\tau}\,U_\delta^{\dagger\,\tau}\big),\quad k = 1,\dots,\lfloor T/\tau\rfloor
equations.description: Between measurements the state evolves unitarily for tau steps; at each measurement the control qubit is measured in the computational basis and the outcome is not post-selected (averaged, giving a dephasing channel on the control). tau = 1 means a measurement after every step; tau >= T recovers the unmeasured algorithm.
equations.abstract_quote: intermediate measurements of the control is presented
equations.justification: Inferred from the stated intermediate measurements of the control and the 'time lapses between measurements'; the computational basis and non-post-selected (ensemble-averaged) treatment are reconstruction choices.
assumptions: Projective measurement in the computational basis of the control
Measurement outcomes are not used for feedback or post-selection; the ensemble-averaged state is tracked

equations.label: Success probability at the marked vertex
equations.description: Probability that a final measurement of the position register at time t yields the marked vertex.
equations.abstract_quote: finding close relationships between probabilities and correlations
equations.justification: The abstract refers to probabilities in a quantum search; the success probability at the marked vertex is the standard quantity, here written for the mixed state produced by eq_3.
assumptions: The 'probabilities' in the abstract refer (at least) to the success probability of locating the marked vertex

equations.label: Control-walker mutual information
equations.description: Quantum mutual information between the control qubit C and the walker W = coin ⊗ position, evaluated on the state of eq_3.
equations.justification: The abstract names 'Mutual Information' as one correlation measure; this is its standard quantum definition. The 'Cumulative Correlation Measure' is not defined in the abstract and is not reconstructed.
assumptions: Mutual information is computed between the control qubit and the remaining registers; the exact bipartition used by the paper is not stated

equations.label: Optimal time and scaling exponent (order estimate)
equations.latex: T^*(N) = \arg\max_{0\le t\le T} P_w(t),\qquad T^*(N) \approx a\,N^{\alpha}\ \Rightarrow\ \alpha \approx \frac{\Delta \log T^*(N)}{\Delta \log N},\qquad \alpha|_{\tau=1} \approx 1
equations.description: The order of the algorithm is estimated from the growth of the optimal search time with N via a log-log fit; the abstract states that measuring at every step (tau = 1) yields O(N) scaling, i.e. alpha ≈ 1, while some tau values improve the performance.
equations.abstract_quote: became of order $O(N)$ (classical brute force search) when the measurement is taken in every step
equations.justification: The abstract states the order is estimated and gives O(N) for tau = 1; the definition of T^* as the first-maximum time and the log-log fit are standard reconstruction choices, the approximate relation is a fit, not an exact equality.
assumptions: Order is estimated from the time to the first maximum of P_w(t); the paper may use a threshold criterion or account for success probability via amplitude amplification

registers.name: control
registers.role: Tulsi's control/ancilla qubit rotated by R_delta and projectively measured every tau steps

registers.name: coin
registers.role: Four-direction coin of the 2D coined walk

registers.name: position
registers.role: Vertex of the 4 x 4 periodic grid (N = 16), x = 4*x_1 + x_2 in binary; marked vertex w

specification.initial_state: |0>_C ⊗ |c_u> ⊗ |s> as in eq_1: control in |0>, coin and position in uniform superposition (7 qubits total for N = 16).

steps.description: Prepare the initial product state with control |0> and uniform superposition on coin and position registers.
Apply tau steps of the Tulsi-like walk unitary U_delta (controlled rotation by delta on the control at the marked vertex, coin, shift).
Measure the control qubit in the computational basis (no post-selection), yielding the dephased joint state; repeat the evolve-tau-steps/measure cycle until T steps are reached.
At each time t record the success probability P_w(t) and the control-walker mutual information I(C:W)_t.
Repeat for several N (and tau) and estimate the scaling exponent alpha from T^*(N).

specification.measurement: Intermediate: computational-basis projective measurement of the single control qubit every tau steps. Final: computational-basis measurement of the position register; success if the outcome equals w (eq_4).
specification.classical_postprocessing: From the recorded P_w(t) determine T^*(N) (first maximum), fit log T^*(N) versus log N to extract alpha for each tau (eq_6); compare the time series of P_w(t) with the correlation measures (eq_5) to identify the relationships referred to in the abstract.
assumptions: No experiment scope was supplied; the N = 16 4 x 4 grid, 2-qubit Grover coin, single marked vertex and tau in {1, 2, T} were chosen as the smallest useful instance
The step unitary of eq_2 is a schematic Tulsi-like controlled-rotation walk; the exact operator of Tulsi's algorithm and the paper's modification are not reproduced from source
The angular parameter delta is left as a free parameter because the abstract states a 'different choice' without giving it
Control measurements are modeled as non-post-selected projective measurements (dephasing channel on the control)
Order estimation uses the first-maximum time of the success probability
missing_information: Exact form of Tulsi's step operator used in the paper (how the control qubit conditions the coin/shift)
The paper's specific 'different choice' of the angular parameter delta and its dependence on N
Definition of the Cumulative Correlation Measure
The set of time lapses tau and sizes N studied, and the resulting numerical probabilities, correlations and order estimates for tau > 1
Whether measurement outcomes of the control are post-selected or used for feedback
Whether the initial control state and measurement basis match this reconstruction
